boundary: which allocator owns the object the defect touches: pymalloc (nested) or libc malloc (non-nested). Decided per case by MEASUREMENT, not by the object's size -- the ASan heap report is run twice and the question is whether it SURVIVES PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc
title: CPython 3.13.7 spatial defects at the pymalloc boundary, plus temporal and spatial defects whose memory comes straight from libc malloc
note: A sibling of pymalloc-repros. That corpus is scoped to consumer-side TEMPORAL defects whose memory comes from pymalloc and asserts completeness for that cell (20 cases, expect_live_in_pin {true: 20}, a shape_prose regex on "[Tt]wenty reports"), so cases here were not added there. 32 cases from 31 upstream fixes (03 and 04 are two triggers for gh-140492). Cases 01-21 are the three cells pymalloc-repros does not cover: 13 spatial/nested, 5 spatial/non-nested, 3 temporal/non-nested. Cases 22-32 are 11 temporal/nested defects, the same upstream issues pymalloc-repros holds as C models (each carries a sibling_issue pointer), here because a C model and an interpreter run of one defect are not the same measurement -- on the base arm the C models all complete while three of the eleven fault, all with cause 24; the two corpora's numbers must not be pooled. Liveness and the nested/non-nested side are both measured on the pinned ASan build. The arms are named as pymalloc-repros names them: spatial is base Capstone (level0 heap, per-object bounds, pymalloc stock via patch 0009; nothing in it revokes heap memory), sublet is the same level0 heap plus patch 0014 (pymalloc's blocks and its >512-byte fallback issued and revoked). Measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-09 over the same 29 cases per arm: base 14/29, sublet 27/29, cheribsd-revocation 11/29; probe/counts.py derives these from results/20261006/matrix.tsv. The cheribsd binary hashes were reconstructed after the runs; see results/20261006/README.md.
